- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below true low.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to align with true mean.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3), model often overestimates upward momentum — cap forecast increase to 1–3% above recent high.  
- Model underestimates true volatility in sentiment-driven periods — add 1–2% buffer to forecast range when sentiment swings >0.4.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is trending downward, model often lags — shift forecast 1–2 days earlier to match sentiment momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.4 → +0.3 → -0.4), model overfits to recent highs — reduce forecast peak by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
